verdict.summary: Creating an app and installing it in your own workspace is quick. Public distribution to other workspaces needs no review, but a Marketplace listing needs 10 active installs and a multi-week review. Unlisted commercial apps also face tighter rate limits on conversations.history.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours to distribute unlisted; several days to prepare a Marketplace submission
verdict.approval_wait: none for unlisted public distribution; Marketplace: up to 10 business days preliminary plus up to 10 weeks functional

gates.name: Development workspace install
gates.unlocks: Install and use the app in the workspace that owns it.
limits: Newly created apps can only be installed in the owning workspace
Workspace admins may restrict installs or require approval; internal apps are still allowed

gates.name: Activate Public Distribution (unlisted)
gates.unlocks: Install in any workspace via the Add to Slack button or a shareable install URL.
limits: Needs SSL on OAuth redirect, interaction, options-load and Events API URLs
Unlisted commercially distributed apps created after May 29, 2025 get conversations.history and conversations.replies capped at 1 request/min and 15 objects per request
Slack says commercial distribution should go through the Marketplace
Workspace admins may require approval of installs
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes to hours; reportedly immediate with no review

gates.name: Slack Marketplace listing
gates.unlocks: Marketplace listing and removal of the unlisted-app rate limits.
limits: Needs at least 10 active workspaces (used in past 28 days), kept through the whole review
Preliminary review up to 10 business days; functional review up to 10 weeks (6 weeks for resubmissions of published apps)
Resubmitting during the preliminary review resets queue place
gates.time_to_reach: Weeks to months after reaching 10 active installs

steps.title: Create the Slack app
steps.detail: Sign in at api.slack.com/apps, create a new app, enter an App Name and pick the Development Workspace.

steps.title: Create a Composio Slack auth config
steps.detail: In Composio, create a custom auth config for the slack toolkit and copy its callback URL. Start on managed auth to test first if you only need your own workspace.

steps.title: Set the Redirect URL and scopes
steps.detail: In OAuth & Permissions, add the redirect URL (HTTPS, no # anchor) and the bot or user scopes you need. Request only scopes you use; the Composio default list is broad.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: If several Redirect URLs are configured, redirect_uri must be identical in the authorize and access steps or you get bad_redirect_uri
Scopes added later require existing installs to reinstall

steps.title: Add client ID and secret to Composio, then install
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the app's Basic Information into the Composio auth config and connect your own account. The authorize endpoint is slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize and the code is exchanged at oauth.v2.access.
gotchas: The authorization code expires after ten minutes
Without token rotation, tokens do not expire

steps.title: Decide on token rotation
steps.detail: Token rotation is optional. If enabled, access tokens expire every 12 hours and refresh tokens are single-use. Only enable it once your refresh handling is ready.
gotchas: Cannot be turned off once on
Marketplace-published apps enable it under Published App Settings

steps.title: Activate Public Distribution
steps.detail: In Manage Distribution, complete the checklist and click Activate Public Distribution to get an Add to Slack button and install URL. Make sure all your callback and event URLs use SSL.
gotchas: Before this, installing in another workspace fails with invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app
Review the 1 request/min limit on conversations.history for unlisted commercial apps

steps.title: Trim scopes for Marketplace
steps.detail: Draft a scope list and a justification for each scope. Remove search:read, admin.*, unused user-token scopes and any scopes for unbuilt features. Mark scopes needed for core function as required. Expect enhanced review if you keep search:read.*, *:history or files:read.
gotchas: Unapproved scopes on a published app cause unapproved_scope errors at install

steps.title: Prepare listing assets and policies
steps.detail: Draft a public landing page (no login) linking to a privacy policy, a support channel answering within 2 business days, a short description of 10 words or fewer, and 1600x1000 images.

steps.title: Reach 10 active workspaces and test
steps.detail: Get at least 10 workspaces actively using the app and keep them there through review. Test install and uninstall on a non-development workspace, and prepare test accounts for any third-party services, since Slack won't use your workspace.

steps.title: Record a demo video and submit
steps.detail: Record a video of install, OAuth, setup, functionality and uninstall, then submit for Marketplace review. Avoid unneeded resubmissions during the preliminary review.

steps.title: Wait for review
steps.detail: Preliminary review takes up to 10 business days, then the functional review up to 10 weeks. Respond to feedback and stay above 10 installs.

requirements.detail: OAuth redirect, interaction request, options-load and Events API URLs must use SSL.
Active means used in the past 28 days, held through the whole review.
Dedicated page, reachable without login, linking to a privacy policy.
Covers data collected, use, retention, and access/transfer/deletion requests, with an email or webform contact.
No extra account needed; responses within 2 business days.
Images 1600x1000 (jpg/png under 2MB); description 10 words or fewer; optional 30-90s YouTube video.
Each scope must relate to testable functionality.
Must 302-redirect to a fully qualified slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize URL.
Provide an install method and third-party test accounts; Slack can't use your workspaces.

scopes.effect: Named in Marketplace guidelines as unsuitable without a clear use case; part of Composio's default list.

scopes.scope: search:read.* (public, private, im, mpim, files, users)

scopes.effect: Enhanced review; broad message access unlikely to be approved without a clear case.
Unlikely to be approved outside Slack's partner program.
Only allowed when the app acts as the authenticating user; unnecessary use gets returned.
No tier detail in findings; each still needs a justification.

blockers.cause: App was never distributed and is being authorized in a workspace other than the one that created it.
blockers.fix: Complete the checklist and click Activate Public Distribution under Manage Distribution.

blockers.cause: Unlisted commercially distributed app created after May 29, 2025, or new installs of older ones.
blockers.fix: Get Marketplace approval, or keep use internal. Whether older existing installs are now capped is unresolved.

blockers.cause: Multiple Redirect URLs configured and redirect_uri differs between authorize and access steps, or does not match.
blockers.fix: Send the identical redirect_uri in both steps, matching a configured URL.

blockers.symptom: unapproved_scope on install of a published app
blockers.cause: Requested scopes are still under review or never submitted.
blockers.fix: Request only approved scopes or submit the new scopes for review.

blockers.cause: Fewer than 10 active workspaces, or app not fully functional and tested on a non-dev workspace.
blockers.fix: Reach and hold 10 active installs and test install/uninstall first.

blockers.cause: Coded workflow apps, or apps providing only an MCP server without in-Slack functionality, are excluded.
blockers.fix: Add in-Slack functionality or stay unlisted.

composio.note: Start on Composio managed OAuth to test quickly. Managed auth does not change Slack's gates: an app is installable elsewhere only after public distribution is activated, and Marketplace listing still needs Slack review. Use your own client ID/secret for your own branding or a listing. The default scope list includes search:read, search:read.*, *:history and files:read, so trim it for a Marketplace-bound app.

open_questions: Whether existing installs of unlisted commercial apps are now capped at 1 request/min on conversations.history (FAQ said March 3, 2026; later page says unaffected).
No published workspace-count cap for unlisted distribution was found.
Developer account prerequisites (plan, partner program, business verification) were not confirmed.
Exact Manage Distribution checklist items and the submission-page wait estimate were not viewed.
How Composio stores and refreshes Slack tokens was not checked.
PKCE details (now GA) were not read.
Partner program terms and whether they lift the admin.* restriction were not read.
